category_title: Students who engage in off-task behavior to obtain teacher and peer attention
minimal_context: Jose is assigned to complete a worksheet at his desk during independent work time in his fourth-grade classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Jose, it is time for independent work. Please complete this worksheet at your desk.

STUDENT: (Pushes the worksheet aside and starts playing with books and materials on his desk.)

TUTOR: You need to focus on your seatwork right now.

STUDENT: (Leaves his desk and walks across the classroom to sharpen his pencil.)

TUTOR: Please go back to your assigned area and finish the worksheet.

STUDENT: (Instead of returning to his desk, he moves around the classroom, talking to peers and interrupting other students who are working.)

options.A: Directly intervene and tell the peers he is interrupting that they need to stop.
options.B: Cue Jose to evaluate his performance of targeted behaviors using a self-management system.
options.C: Agree with Jose that he is having a rough time with the independent work.
options.D: Provide a detailed instruction of each specific element in the independent work task.
